title: POC Weekly - Latency Tuning (RiverMark)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on TTFT improvements via streaming and kernel tuning. Miguel walked through kernel profiling and prefix/KV caching results; Priya agreed to share prompt histograms. Action items: profiling run, prompt set, pricing & SOC2 docs.
topics: Sequence length distribution and kernel selection
action_items: Miguel Santos: run kernel-level profiler on RiverMark 4k-sequence workload and share flamegraphs by 2027-03-26
Priya Nair: upload representative prompt set and sequence length histogram to shared drive by 2027-03-25
Lara Chen: send updated Dedicated pilot pricing, SOC2 pack, and kernel tuning notes by 2027-03-24
next_steps: Run 24h latency stress run on hosted region with streaming+prefix caching enabled (Redwood)
Customer to validate tail-latency in their staging infra with the provided inference script
Schedule tech deep-dive next week if profiling shows kernel bottlenecks
meeting_header: Date: 2027-03-23 | Time: 10:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Redwood: Lara Chen, Miguel Santos | RiverMark: Priya Nair, Jonah Lee, Sofia Morales
notes: Customer still sensitive to TTFT for interactive workflows (target <200ms). They prefer hosted pilot but evaluating Dedicated if tail-latency / cost tradeoffs favor it. SOC2 + network diagram remains blocking for enterprise procurement.
transcript:
[00:00] Lara Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Priya Nair: Priya here, hi.
[00:09] Jonah Lee: Jonah on infra.
[00:11] Sofia Morales: Sofia, product.
[00:13] Miguel Santos: Mig here, SE on the account.
[00:16] Lara Chen: Cool, agenda is TTFT numbers, streaming tests, kernel profiling, and next steps. Miguel you want to start?
[00:27] Miguel Santos: Yeah, sure. So we ran the two configs you asked for — baseline non-streaming and streaming with prefix caching. Baseline, the median TTFT was ~320ms, p95 about 670ms on your 2k token workload. With streaming enabled and aggressive prefix/KV caching we saw median TTFT drop to ~165ms, p95 to ~380ms.
[00:49] Priya Nair: Wait 165ms median, that's huge improvement. Are you talking about first byte or first token?
[00:55] Miguel Santos: First token, TTFT first token, sorry. There's some noise depending on sequence length — short prompts see sub-120ms. Longer 3-4k sequences push up kernel scheduling overhead.
[01:10] Jonah Lee: How did you account for network latency? Our staging is in us-east-1, we usually see 50-70ms to endpoints.
[01:16] Miguel Santos: These numbers are from the hosted region closest to you; we stripped out client-side NLB so they are server-side TTFT. Add your network egress for end-to-end.
[01:26] Sofia Morales: Were models quantized? We saw some accuracy diffs earlier.
[01:29] Miguel Santos: We tested both fp16 and 4-bit quant profiles. 4-bit QAT-ish profile gave ~1-2% delta on rouge/ut — generally acceptable for retrieval-augmented responses; we can pin to fp16 if you need zero regression.
[01:45] Lara Chen: Can you walk through kernel profiling results?
[01:48] Miguel Santos: Sure — we ran nvprof and our internal kernel tracer. Biggest hotspot was attention kernel for long seqs, and some memcpy/transpose ops in the head. On the 4k sequence trace, attention time is ~58% of token time; kernel launch overhead accumulates.
[02:10] Priya Nair: So is that a runtime thing we can tune by changing kernel selection or sequence packing?
[02:15] Miguel Santos: Both. The runtime can pick alternative attention kernels optimized for longer sequences — cost is sometimes slightly higher per-token but reduces launch overhead. Also packing multiple requests into a continous batch helps but we know you have real-time constraints so batching window is limited.
[02:29] Jonah Lee: Any quick wins we can flip now?
[02:32] Miguel Santos: Yes — enable streaming (we did), enable prefix/KV caching (we did), and reduce max output chunk size to 8 tokens to get earlier first token. Also use the small kernel path for short sequences. We'll share a runtime config snippet.
[02:47] Priya Nair: How about the memory usage when we enable KV caching, for long sessions? Concerned about GPU memory footprint.
[02:52] Miguel Santos: KV cache grows linearly with sequence length; in our tests a 4k seq used ~28GB of GPU mem on the model we used. For Hosted we recommend session-level eviction policies and per-customer caps. For Dedicated we can provision larger GPU sets.
[03:10] Sofia Morales: Is there an observable cost delta for enabling streaming vs non-streaming?
[03:14] Miguel Santos: Streaming slightly increases per-request overhead but reduces perceived latency; overall token cost is similar. If you enable streaming with smaller chunk sizes you may see more API calls but token billing stays the same—though if you enable extra retries it can add.
[03:29] Lara Chen: Priya, you mentioned you have a representative prompt set — did you get a chance to run it with our script?
[03:35] Priya Nair: Not yet, we have a histogram of seq lengths but not the full prompt set uploaded. Will do by Thursday.
[03:41] Miguel Santos: Perfect; that histogram will let us pick the best kernel profiles.
[03:45] [04:00] Miguel Santos: Also note, for tail latency you might want to use model routing — smaller-capacity model variant for cold starts, fallback to bigger model for quality. That avoids some cold-cache TTFT spikes.
[04:15] Jonah Lee: Can Redwood do warm standby instances to reduce cold starts?
[04:18] Miguel Santos: Yes, Dedicated can reserve hot instances; Hosted can do warm pools with warmup pinging but it's not free. We'll include warm-pool sizing in the pricing.
[04:30] Priya Nair: About kernel selection — you mentioned alternative attention kernels, are these proprietary to Redwood runtime or open ones?
[04:36] Miguel Santos: Our runtime selects kernels from a set — some are vendor optimized (cuBLAS/cuda) and others are our tuned kernels for transformer-attention. For some models the vendor kernels are faster for long seqs, for others our fused kernels are better. We can share profiler outputs showing per-kernel times.
[04:58] Lara Chen: Any stability issues when switching kernels mid-rollout?
[05:02] Miguel Santos: No major ones; runtime does canary kernel swaps and we have deterministic fallbacks. We recommend a canary rollout on a small traffic percentage first.
[05:12] Sofia Morales: On the security side, procurement needs SOC2, SAML SSO, and network diagram with private link. Status?
[05:19] Lara Chen: I'll send SOC2 and SAML docs after the call. We have a VPC private link option in Private deployment.
[05:26] Priya Nair: Good. For the pilot we want hosted but with VPC peering, if possible.
[05:31] Miguel Santos: We can do Hosted with private networking for the pilot — it's a common pattern. We may need to open endpoints and set IP allowlist.
[05:40] [06:00] Miguel Santos: Back to numbers: we instrumented streaming chunk sizes 4,8,16 tokens. 8 token chunk gave the best TTFT vs throughput balance for your workload. 4 token reduced TTFT another 20-30ms but increased request overhead significantly.
[06:20] Priya Nair: What about model quantization impact on TTFT? 4-bit reduces kernel time but sometimes increases compute due to dequant/quant overhead?
[06:27] Miguel Santos: Right — 4-bit helps memory and raw compute on some kernels but adds dequant overhead on others; net TTFT may improve or slightly worsen depending on kernel. For your end-to-end we saw median unchanged but p95 got slightly better with 4-bit when combined with streaming.
[06:45] Jonah Lee: Any specific logs we should collect to validate tail-latency in our infra?
[06:49] Miguel Santos: Collect server-side TTFT, kernel-level timings (we'll give profiler tags), and client-side RTT. Also collect sequence length and cache-hit flags for prefix cache.
[07:05] Lara Chen: Let's talk about the long-run: if we move to Dedicated, how does provisioning change?
[07:10] Miguel Santos: Dedicated allows reserved GPU pools, warm standby hot slots, and custom autoscaling policies. It removes noisy neighbor concerns and gives predictable tail-latency. Cost is upfront, but if you're at consistent throughput it's more economical.
[07:25] Priya Nair: Do you have an estimate to hit our SLAs — we want p95 < 400ms for 80% of traffic.
end_transcript:
[07:32] Miguel Santos: With streaming+prefix caching and warm pools, our projection for your traffic shape is p95 ~340-380ms on Hosted; Dedicated should tighten that to ~300-350ms depending on slot sizing. We'll model this in the pricing doc.
[07:48] Sofia Morales: Any regressions observed in NLG quality when using kernels optimized for speed?
[07:52] Miguel Santos: Minimal; we typically see minor syntactic differences but semantics preserved. We'll add your eval prompts to a regression suite.
[07:59] [08:30] Miguel Santos: Quick demo of flamegraph — (screen share) you can see attention peaks, and the memcpy/transpose lines. If we redirect to an alt-kernel the attention bar halves on long seqs.
[08:52] Priya Nair: Is it possible to run a custom kernel we have internally?
[08:56] Miguel Santos: We can plugin custom kernels if they meet ABI expectations; it's an enterprise workflow and requires testing.
[09:04] Jonah Lee: For the 24h stress run, what throughput should we target?
[09:09] Lara Chen: Priya, what are your production request QPS numbers?
[09:12] Priya Nair: Peak is about 120 QPS, median 35 QPS. For pilot let's target 60 QPS sustained to start.
[09:20] Miguel Santos: Good — we'll run a 24h at 60 QPS with your prompt histogram and streaming enabled. We'll publish TTFT, p50/p95/p99, and kernel profiles.
[09:32] Sofia Morales: Any caveats about sequence packing or request multiplexing that could distort latency?
[09:37] Miguel Santos: If we pack requests to increase throughput it changes first-token timing; for accurate TTFT measurement we should keep 1:1 request-to-inference in the stress run.
[09:49] [10:00] Lara Chen: Ok, recap — Miguel will run profiling + 24h run, Priya upload prompt set, Lara send docs and pricing. Anything else?
[10:08] Priya Nair: Could you include a rough cost comparison of Hosted vs Dedicated for our 60 QPS profile?
[10:12] Lara Chen: Yep, I'll include that in the pricing note.
[10:15] Jonah Lee: One more thing — can you annotate the benchmark sheet with kernel names so our infra team can cross-check?
[10:20] Miguel Santos: Will do. We'll include kernel name, version, and flags used.
[10:24] [11:00] Sofia Morales: Timeline — we aim to decide pilot go/no-go by April 6.
[11:06] Lara Chen: Sounds good. Anything else?
[11:09] Priya Nair: No, that's it thanks.
[11:11] Miguel Santos: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and action items.
[11:15] Lara Chen: End.

Note: transcription contains occasional mis-hear — e.g., KV cache sometimes transcribed as KV cash. References posted to shared drive after call.
